stem: A nurse explains routine newborn hearing screening to new parents. Which statement is accurate?

options.A: Only newborns with a documented family history of childhood hearing loss need screening.
options.B: All newborns should complete hearing screening by 1 month of age so possible hearing loss can be identified and followed promptly.
options.C: Hearing screening should wait until speech delay becomes apparent in early childhood.
options.D: Routine screening is unnecessary because congenital hearing loss cannot be detected in the newborn period.

rationale: CDC Early Hearing Detection and Intervention guidance uses the 1-3-6 benchmarks: hearing screening by 1 month of age, diagnostic evaluation by 3 months for infants who do not pass, and enrollment in early intervention by 6 months when hearing loss is diagnosed. CDC specifically directs health professionals to ensure the hearing-screening process is complete for all newborns. B is correct.
educational_objective: Explain the universal newborn hearing-screening benchmark and the importance of timely follow-up when a newborn does not pass screening.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Information About Hearing Loss in Children for Health Professionals
source_locator: What health professionals can do — No later than 1 month of age; EHDI 1-3-6 benchmarks
source_claim_supported: CDC directs health professionals to ensure the hearing-screening process is complete for all newborns by 1 month, with diagnostic evaluation by 3 months for infants who do not pass and timely intervention thereafter.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Printed p.9, Health Promotion and Maintenance — newborn care, screening, and age-appropriate preventive care
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — newborn hearing screening

source_original.stem: A nurse is explaining the purpose of routine newborn hearing screening to new parents. The nurse should explain that this screening is important because:

options.A: Screen only newborns with a documented family history of childhood hearing loss
options.B: Screen all newborns so hearing loss can be identified and addressed early
options.C: Delay hearing screening until speech delay becomes apparent in early childhood
options.D: Omit routine screening because congenital hearing loss is too uncommon to screen

source_original.rationale: Routine newborn hearing screening (recommended for all infants, typically before hospital discharge) allows for early identification of hearing loss, which is important because timely intervention (before 6 months of age, when possible) significantly supports optimal speech, language, and cognitive development, given the critical early window for auditory-based learning.
source_original.source_detail: All infants should be screened for hearing loss before 1 month of age; May 7, 2025 page, accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Retained universal newborn screening, replaced the original vague rationale with CDC's exact 1-3-6 benchmark language, and avoided overstating developmental effect size or an absolute before-discharge requirement.

audit_findings.source_authority: CDC EHDI guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: CDC EHDI health-professional guidance remained current and accessible on 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Universal newborn screening and the 1-month benchmark were directly verified; follow-up timing was kept within CDC's 1-3-6 framework.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because CDC guidance applies to all newborns, not only those with family history.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because screening is recommended in the newborn period rather than after speech delay.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because newborn hearing screening is established and feasible.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B matches universal screening and the CDC benchmark.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are framed as screening policies; no wording cue independently reveals the key.
audit_findings.blueprint: Newborn screening and anticipatory preventive care map to Health Promotion and Maintenance.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked CDC's health-professional and screening pages; universal newborn screening by 1 month remained the supported answer.
